title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for alcohol use disorder.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman who presents for a scheduled follow-up regarding her history of alcohol use disorder, moderate. She reports that she has successfully abstained from alcohol for over a year. She denies any current cravings or difficulties maintaining her sobriety. She reports feeling stable and continues to participate in her routine activities without issues.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and is in no acute distress. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is warm and dry. Gait is steady and balanced. Speech is clear and coherent.

Assessment
1. Alcohol use disorder, moderate. The patient is currently in sustained remission. She demonstrates excellent self-management and has maintained sobriety for more than twelve months.

Plan
1. Continue current plan of abstinence.
2. Schedule follow-up in six months to monitor continued stability and support her ongoing recovery.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, moderate or severe, in remission: F10.21, alcohol dependence in remission (HCC 139).

distractors.why: Moderate or severe use disorder is dependence (F10.2-).

hccs.label: Alcohol Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Alcohol Use with Specified Non-Psychotic Complications
